headline: ASML, the Dutch maker of chip-making machines, says AI-driven demand for its machines is so strong that it will not be able to fully supply its customers in 2027 or 2028.
score_reason: Pool score kept: ASML's own statement is confirmed in several reports and the maker of chip-making machines sets the pace of AI chip supply.
importance_line: If ASML is right, the equipment needed to build more AI chips will stay scarce for two more years, which could keep AI services costly for people and businesses and limit how fast chipmakers can expand; these are the company's own forecasts, and the low end of its quarterly range is only just above analysts' expectations.
summary: Reuters reports that ASML, the Dutch maker of the machines that print circuit patterns onto chips, said on 14 Oct 2026 that it is looking at ways to expand capacity further because it cannot fully meet AI-driven demand in 2027 and 2028. It forecast fourth-quarter 2026 sales of €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion, against the €14.19 billion analysts had expected, and Christophe Fouquet, ASML's chief executive, said customers are already discussing orders for 2029 and sometimes 2030.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); text read on RTE.ie and CTech, which carry the same ASML statement. Facts match the Reuters headline.
